title: Trump Names Hardliner Stephen Miller as White House Chief of Staff After Midterm Defeats
snippet: President Donald Trump has appointed longtime architect of his immigration crackdown Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff, signaling a confrontational strategy against a incoming Democratic Congress.
content:
President Donald Trump has named longtime senior advisor Stephen Miller as his next White House chief of staff, sending an unmistakable signal that the administration plans to double down on its hardline agenda despite sweeping Republican losses in the midterm elections.

Miller, 41, will officially take over the position on Monday, replacing Susie Wiles. The leadership shift comes as Trump prepares to face a newly empowered Democratic-led House and Senate, alongside a battery of incoming congressional investigations targeting his administration.

A staunch advocate for expansive executive power, Miller takes control of the West Wing at a moment when legislative avenues for Trump's domestic platform have largely narrowed. According to White House officials, the appointment indicates that Trump has no plans to moderate his policies despite widespread voter pushback.

"He's not changing course," one White House official noted, characterizing the move as a reward for Trump's most loyal strategist.

A Tougher Line on Capitol Hill

The elevation of Miller, renowned for his uncompromising style, suggests a heightened level of friction between the executive branch and lawmakers. Incoming Democratic Speaker of the House Hakeem Jeffries quickly slammed the decision, calling Miller a "reckless extremist."

House Democrats are already signaling plans to launch deep inquiries into Miller's key initiatives. Representative Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the Oversight Committee, publicly warned Miller to prepare for tough congressional scrutiny over his enforcement actions.

Wiles, who became the first woman to serve as chief of staff, submitted her resignation Thursday evening and will transition to managing Trump's political operation. Respected across Washington for bringing order to a routinely turbulent administration, Wiles maintained a disciplined operation while undergoing treatment for early-stage breast cancer earlier this year.

Driving the Administration's Core Agenda

One of the few aides to serve across both of Trump's terms, Miller has exercised wide-ranging influence over domestic policy. As deputy chief of staff, he spearheaded aggressive immigration crackdowns—setting aggressive daily arrest targets that deployed federal agents into communities nationwide, a strategy that public opinion polls show remains broadly unpopular.

Miller has also been instrumental in efforts to overhaul the federal civil service and lead battles against university diversity initiatives. On foreign policy, he has staunchly supported offensive military operations in the Middle East and aggressive naval interdictions in Latin America.

While Trump allies such as Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth celebrated Miller's promotion on social media, political analysts view the move as a sign that the White House is preparing for partisan warfare rather than legislative compromise.
